title: Measures and instruments
description: Standardized and idiographic instruments used in CBT for screening, severity, outcome, process, competence and risk monitoring. Each concept carries page, construct, items (core or main-form item count), format, licensing (public-domain: reproduce without a request; free-with-permission: copyrighted but free for clinical or non-commercial use under stated terms or on request; proprietary: purchase or paid license), licensing_note and population. Used to tag measurement slots and pages.

concepts.label: Patient Health Questionnaire-9 (PHQ-9)
concepts.definition: Nine-item self-report of DSM depressive symptoms over the past two weeks, scored 0 to 27, with severity cutpoints at 5, 10, 15 and 20.
concepts.client_wording: A short questionnaire about how often depression symptoms have bothered you over the last two weeks.
concepts.example: Score 14 (moderate); item 9 is endorsed, so suicide risk is assessed in the same session.
concepts.licensing_note: PHQ Screeners: no permission required to reproduce, translate, display or distribute.

concepts.label: Patient Health Questionnaire-2 (PHQ-2)
concepts.definition: First two PHQ-9 items (depressed mood, loss of interest), scored 0 to 6; a score of 3 or more prompts fuller assessment.
concepts.client_wording: Two quick questions about low mood and loss of interest over the last two weeks.
concepts.example: PHQ-2 score 4 at a primary care visit, so the full PHQ-9 is given.
concepts.licensing_note: PHQ Screeners: no permission required.
concepts.population: Adults; screening in primary care and general settings

concepts.label: Beck Depression Inventory-II (BDI-II)
concepts.definition: Twenty-one-item self-report of depressive symptom severity over the past two weeks, each item 0 to 3, total 0 to 63.
concepts.client_wording: A questionnaire about depression symptoms over the last two weeks.
concepts.example: Intake score in the moderate range falls to the minimal range by session 14.
concepts.licensing_note: Pearson; purchase required (qualification level B). Do not reproduce item wording.

concepts.label: Quick Inventory of Depressive Symptomatology, Self-Report (QIDS-SR16)
concepts.definition: Sixteen-item self-report covering the nine DSM depression domains over the past seven days; highest item per domain is summed, total 0 to 27.
concepts.client_wording: A questionnaire about depression symptoms over the past week.
concepts.example: Total 16 (severe) at baseline; 5 (none) after treatment indicates remission.
concepts.licensing_note: Copyright held by developers; distributed free via ids-qids.org; check terms for commercial use.

concepts.label: Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale (EPDS)
concepts.definition: Ten-item self-report screening for perinatal depression over the past seven days, total 0 to 30; includes one self-harm item.
concepts.client_wording: A short questionnaire about how you have felt over the past week, during or after pregnancy.
concepts.example: Score 14 at six weeks postpartum, and the self-harm item is reviewed immediately.
concepts.licensing_note: Copyright Royal College of Psychiatrists; may be reproduced if authors, title and source are cited.
concepts.population: Pregnant and postpartum people; validated for partners in some studies

concepts.label: Generalized Anxiety Disorder-7 (GAD-7)
concepts.definition: Seven-item self-report of generalized anxiety symptoms over the past two weeks, scored 0 to 21, with cutpoints at 5, 10 and 15.
concepts.client_wording: A short questionnaire about how often anxiety and worry bothered you over the last two weeks.
concepts.example: Score 12 (moderate) at intake; 10 or more prompts assessment for an anxiety disorder.
concepts.construct: Generalized anxiety severity; screens for common anxiety disorders
concepts.licensing_note: PHQ Screeners: no permission required to reproduce, translate, display or distribute.

concepts.label: Generalized Anxiety Disorder-2 (GAD-2)
concepts.definition: First two GAD-7 items (nervousness, uncontrollable worry), scored 0 to 6; a score of 3 or more prompts fuller assessment.
concepts.client_wording: Two quick questions about feeling nervous and being unable to stop worrying.
concepts.example: GAD-2 score 3, so the full GAD-7 is completed.
concepts.licensing_note: PHQ Screeners: no permission required.
concepts.population: Adults; screening in primary care and general settings

concepts.label: Beck Anxiety Inventory (BAI)
concepts.definition: Twenty-one-item self-report of anxiety symptom severity, weighted toward physical symptoms, each item 0 to 3, total 0 to 63.
concepts.client_wording: A questionnaire about anxiety symptoms, especially body symptoms, over the recent past.
concepts.example: High somatic item scores support a panic-focused formulation.
concepts.licensing_note: Pearson; purchase required. Do not reproduce item wording.

concepts.label: Overall Anxiety Severity and Impairment Scale (OASIS)
concepts.definition: Five-item self-report of anxiety frequency, intensity, avoidance and work and social impairment across anxiety disorders over the past week, total 0 to 20.
concepts.client_wording: Five questions about how often anxiety affects you and how much it gets in the way.
concepts.example: Used weekly across a mixed anxiety caseload to track overall change.
concepts.licensing_note: Published in the validation article; confirm terms with authors for commercial use.

concepts.label: Panic Disorder Severity Scale (PDSS)
concepts.definition: Seven-item measure of panic disorder severity: attack frequency, distress, anticipatory anxiety, avoidance and impairment, each 0 to 4, total 0 to 28.
concepts.client_wording: Seven questions about panic attacks, worry about them, avoidance and how they affect your life.
concepts.example: Weekly self-report scores fall from 16 to 5 over interoceptive exposure work.
concepts.licensing_note: Copyright M. K. Shear; free for clinicians in practice and non-industry research; other uses need permission.
concepts.population: Adults with panic disorder; clinician and self-report versions

concepts.label: Anxiety Sensitivity Index-3 (ASI-3)
concepts.definition: Eighteen-item self-report of fear of anxiety-related sensations, with physical, cognitive and social concern subscales, each item 0 to 4.
concepts.client_wording: Questions about how frightening you find the feelings and signs of anxiety.
concepts.example: High physical concerns subscale supports a panic formulation and interoceptive exposure.
concepts.licensing_note: Published in the validation article; free for clinical and research use with citation.

concepts.label: Social Phobia Inventory (SPIN)
concepts.definition: Seventeen-item self-report of social anxiety over the past week covering fear, avoidance and physiological symptoms, each item 0 to 4, total 0 to 68.
concepts.client_wording: Questions about fear and avoidance of social situations and body symptoms over the past week.
concepts.example: Score 42 at intake supports a social anxiety disorder assessment.
concepts.licensing_note: Copyright J. R. T. Davidson; permission and a user fee may be required from the copyright holder.

concepts.label: Liebowitz Social Anxiety Scale (LSAS)
concepts.definition: Rates 24 social and performance situations separately for fear or anxiety and avoidance, each 0 to 3, giving subscale and total scores.
concepts.client_wording: A list of social and performance situations rated for how anxious you feel and how much you avoid them.
concepts.example: Avoidance subscale highlights eating in public and speaking to authority figures as exposure targets.
concepts.licensing_note: Copyright M. R. Liebowitz; distributed via Mapi Research Trust; confirm terms before use.
concepts.population: Adults; child and adolescent version (LSAS-CA) exists

concepts.label: Short Health Anxiety Inventory (SHAI)
concepts.definition: Eighteen-item self-report of health anxiety: 14 items on illness worry and likelihood plus 4 on feared negative consequences, total 0 to 54.
concepts.client_wording: Questions about worry about your health and what being ill would mean for you.
concepts.example: Score well above the clinical range with frequent body checking supports a health anxiety formulation.
concepts.licensing_note: Copyright held by the authors; published in the validation article.
concepts.population: Adults; clinical, community and medical samples

concepts.label: Penn State Worry Questionnaire (PSWQ)
concepts.definition: Sixteen-item self-report of trait worry, its excessiveness, pervasiveness and uncontrollability, each item 1 to 5, total 16 to 80.
concepts.client_wording: Questions about how much you tend to worry and how hard it is to stop.
concepts.example: Score 68 supports pathological worry as a primary treatment target.
concepts.licensing_note: Published in the original article; widely reproduced for clinical use.

concepts.label: Intolerance of Uncertainty Scale-12 (IUS-12)
concepts.definition: Twelve-item short form measuring reactions to uncertainty, with prospective and inhibitory anxiety factors, each item 1 to 5, total 12 to 60.
concepts.client_wording: Questions about how you react when things are uncertain or unpredictable.
concepts.example: High inhibitory subscale suggests uncertainty leads to freezing and avoidance.
concepts.licensing_note: Published in the validation article; free for clinical and research use with citation.

concepts.label: Hospital Anxiety and Depression Scale (HADS)
concepts.definition: Fourteen-item self-report with seven anxiety and seven depression items, designed to limit overlap with physical illness symptoms.
concepts.client_wording: Short questions about anxiety and low mood, designed for people with physical health problems.
concepts.example: Used in a cardiac rehabilitation service to screen for anxiety and depression.
concepts.construct: Anxiety and depression in medical settings
concepts.licensing_note: Copyright held by the authors; licensed commercially; check the current distributor before use.
concepts.population: Adults with physical illness; general adult use

concepts.label: Depression Anxiety Stress Scales-21 (DASS-21)
concepts.definition: Twenty-one-item short form of the DASS with seven-item depression, anxiety and stress scales over the past week; scores doubled to match DASS-42 norms.
concepts.client_wording: Questions about low mood, anxiety and stress over the past week.
concepts.example: Stress subscale is elevated while depression is normal, guiding focus on tension and irritability.
concepts.licensing_note: Questionnaire is in the public domain; the manual is sold separately.
concepts.population: Adults; also used with older adolescents

concepts.label: Screen for Child Anxiety Related Disorders (SCARED)
concepts.definition: Forty-one-item child and parent report of anxiety symptoms with five factors paralleling DSM anxiety disorders, each item 0 to 2.
concepts.client_wording: Questions for you or your parent about worries and fears.
concepts.example: Separation anxiety subscale is elevated on both child and parent forms.
concepts.construct: Child and adolescent anxiety disorder symptoms
concepts.licensing_note: Copyright held by the developers; free at no cost from the University of Pittsburgh.
concepts.population: Ages 8 to 18; child and parent forms

concepts.label: Revised Child Anxiety and Depression Scale (RCADS)
concepts.definition: Forty-seven-item youth or parent report with subscales for separation, social, generalized, panic and obsessive-compulsive anxiety and major depression.
concepts.client_wording: Questions for you or your parent about worries, fears and low mood.
concepts.example: Major depression and social anxiety subscales are both elevated in a 14-year-old.
concepts.construct: Child and adolescent anxiety and depression symptoms
concepts.licensing_note: Copyright Chorpita and Spence; free under a limited license; commercial use or resale prohibited.
concepts.population: School-age children and adolescents; youth and parent forms

concepts.label: Spence Children's Anxiety Scale (SCAS)
concepts.definition: Forty-four-item child report (38 scored, 6 filler, each 0 to 3) with six anxiety subscales; parent and preschool versions exist.
concepts.client_wording: Questions for you or your parent about worries and fears.
concepts.example: Separation anxiety subscale T-score above 60 on both child and parent forms.
sources: SCAS-Site § SCAS child overview; Scoring and interpretation; Home page, permissions
concepts.licensing_note: Copyright Spence; free for researchers and individual practitioners; services, agencies and commercial users need permission or a license; do not modify.
concepts.population: Children and adolescents; child, parent and preschool versions

concepts.label: PTSD Checklist for DSM-5 (PCL-5)
concepts.definition: Twenty-item self-report of DSM-5 PTSD symptoms over the past month, each 0 to 4, total 0 to 80; a provisional cutpoint of 31 to 33.
concepts.client_wording: Questions about how much trauma-related problems bothered you over the past month.
concepts.example: Score falls from 52 to 24, a drop of more than 10 points, indicating response.
concepts.construct: PTSD symptom severity (DSM-5 clusters B to E)
concepts.licensing_note: National Center for PTSD: public domain, not copyrighted; intended for qualified professionals.

concepts.label: Clinician-Administered PTSD Scale for DSM-5 (CAPS-5)
concepts.definition: Thirty-item structured clinical interview assessing the 20 DSM-5 PTSD symptoms, onset, duration, distress, impairment and dissociative subtype; 45 to 60 minutes.
concepts.client_wording: A structured interview about trauma-related symptoms and how they affect you.
concepts.example: Used to confirm a PTSD diagnosis before starting trauma-focused therapy.
concepts.licensing_note: Free on request from the National Center for PTSD for qualified clinicians and researchers.
concepts.population: Adults; child and adolescent version (CAPS-CA-5) for ages 7 and up

concepts.label: International Trauma Questionnaire (ITQ)
concepts.definition: Eighteen-item self-report of ICD-11 PTSD and complex PTSD: six PTSD items, six disturbances in self-organization items, and six functional impairment items.
concepts.client_wording: Questions about trauma-related symptoms and difficulties with emotions, self-worth and relationships.
concepts.example: Criteria met for complex PTSD, so the plan adds emotion regulation and relationship work.
concepts.licensing_note: Freely available in the public domain.
concepts.population: Adults; child and caregiver versions (ITQ-CA, ITQ-CC) exist

concepts.label: Yale-Brown Obsessive Compulsive Scale (Y-BOCS)
concepts.definition: Clinician-rated interview with a symptom checklist and 10 severity items (five obsessions, five compulsions), each 0 to 4, total 0 to 40.
concepts.client_wording: An interview about obsessions and compulsions and how much they affect your life.
concepts.example: Score falls from 26 to 12 over a course of ERP.
concepts.licensing_note: Copyrighted; licensed through the distributor. Do not reproduce item wording.

concepts.label: Obsessive-Compulsive Inventory-Revised (OCI-R)
concepts.definition: Eighteen-item self-report of OCD symptom distress with six subscales: washing, checking, ordering, obsessing, hoarding and neutralizing; total 0 to 72.
concepts.client_wording: Questions about how much different obsessions and compulsions have distressed you in the past month.
concepts.example: High checking and obsessing subscales guide the exposure hierarchy.
concepts.licensing_note: Published in the validation article; free for clinical and research use with citation.

concepts.label: Dimensional Obsessive-Compulsive Scale (DOCS)
concepts.definition: Twenty-item self-report rating severity across four OCD dimensions: contamination, responsibility for harm, unacceptable thoughts, and symmetry; total 0 to 80.
concepts.client_wording: Questions about four common types of obsessions and compulsions and how much they affect you.
concepts.example: Highest score is the unacceptable thoughts dimension, pointing to mental rituals.
concepts.licensing_note: Published in the validation article; free for clinical and research use with citation.

concepts.label: Saving Inventory-Revised (SI-R)
concepts.definition: Twenty-three-item self-report of hoarding with clutter, difficulty discarding and excessive acquisition subscales.
concepts.client_wording: Questions about clutter, difficulty letting go of things, and acquiring things.
concepts.example: Clutter subscale is high; difficulty discarding is the main treatment focus.
concepts.licensing_note: Published in the validation article; free for clinical and research use with citation.

concepts.label: Eating Disorder Examination Questionnaire (EDE-Q 6.0)
concepts.definition: Twenty-eight-item self-report over the past 28 days: 22 items forming restraint, eating, shape and weight concern subscales, plus six behavior frequencies.
concepts.client_wording: Questions about eating, body shape and weight concerns, and eating behaviors over the past four weeks.
concepts.example: Global score 4.1 with weekly objective binges; shape concern is the highest subscale.
concepts.licensing_note: Copyright held by the authors; free for non-commercial use without seeking permission; commercial use by agreement.

concepts.label: Adult ADHD Self-Report Scale v1.1 (ASRS)
concepts.definition: WHO 18-item self-report of DSM ADHD symptom frequency over six months; the first six items (Part A) form the screener.
concepts.client_wording: Questions about how often attention, organization and restlessness difficulties happen for you.
concepts.example: Part A screener is positive, so a full ADHD assessment with collateral history is arranged.
concepts.licensing_note: Copyright WHO; six-item screener free unaltered with copyright notice; 18-item checklist requires permission.

concepts.label: Conners Adult ADHD Rating Scales, 2nd Edition (CAARS 2)
concepts.definition: Normed adult ADHD rating scales with self and observer forms (97 items each), short forms and a 12-item ADHD Index, including impairment items.
concepts.client_wording: Questions for you and someone who knows you well about attention, activity and impulsivity.
concepts.example: Self and partner ratings both elevated on inattention, supporting the diagnostic assessment.
concepts.licensing_note: MHS; purchase required. Do not reproduce item wording.

concepts.label: Conners 4th Edition (Conners 4)
concepts.definition: Normed ADHD rating scales for youth with parent (117 items), teacher (109) and self-report (118) forms, short forms and a 12-item ADHD Index.
concepts.client_wording: Questions for you, your parent and teacher about attention, activity and behavior.
concepts.example: Parent and teacher forms both elevated on inattention across home and school.
concepts.construct: Child and adolescent ADHD symptoms and impairment
concepts.licensing_note: MHS; purchase required. Item count shown is the full parent form.

concepts.label: NICHQ Vanderbilt Assessment Scales
concepts.definition: Parent (55 items) and teacher (43 items) ratings of DSM ADHD symptoms, common comorbid symptoms and school and home performance.
concepts.client_wording: Questions for parents and teachers about a child's attention, behavior and how they are doing.
concepts.example: Teacher form meets inattentive criteria with impaired classwork; parent form is borderline.
concepts.construct: Child ADHD symptoms, comorbidity screen and performance
concepts.licensing_note: Copyright AAP and NICHQ; freely used in clinical practice. Item count shown is the parent form.
concepts.population: Ages 6 to 12; parent and teacher forms

concepts.label: Insomnia Severity Index (ISI)
concepts.definition: Seven-item self-report of insomnia severity, satisfaction, daytime interference, noticeability and distress, each 0 to 4, total 0 to 28.
concepts.client_wording: Seven questions about your sleep problems and how much they affect you.
concepts.example: Score 19 (moderate clinical insomnia) at intake; 7 after CBT-I.
concepts.licensing_note: Copyright C. M. Morin; distributed by Mapi Research Trust; license needed, fees may apply for some uses.

concepts.label: Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI)
concepts.definition: Self-report of sleep quality over the past month: 19 self-rated items forming seven component scores and a global score of 0 to 21.
concepts.client_wording: Questions about your sleep habits and sleep quality over the past month.
concepts.example: Global score 12 indicates poor sleep quality, mainly from long sleep latency.
concepts.licensing_note: Copyright University of Pittsburgh; free for non-commercial use with permission.

concepts.label: Consensus Sleep Diary (CSD)
concepts.definition: Standardized daily sleep diary with nine core items (for example bedtime, sleep latency, awakenings, final wake time, quality) used to calculate sleep parameters.
concepts.client_wording: A daily record you fill in each morning about when and how you slept.
concepts.example: Two weeks of diaries show sleep efficiency of 68%, used to set the sleep window.
concepts.construct: Prospective sleep pattern (sleep latency, wake time, efficiency)
concepts.licensing_note: Published openly for standardized use; no license fee identified.
concepts.population: Adults with insomnia and other sleep complaints

concepts.label: Alcohol Use Disorders Identification Test (AUDIT)
concepts.definition: WHO 10-item screen for hazardous and harmful drinking and dependence, total 0 to 40, with risk zones at 8, 16 and 20.
concepts.client_wording: Ten questions about how much and how often you drink, and its effects.
concepts.example: Score 17 (zone III), so brief intervention plus monitoring and further assessment are offered.
concepts.licensing_note: WHO: may be freely reproduced and translated; not for sale or commercial use.
concepts.population: Adults; primary care and general settings

concepts.label: AUDIT-Consumption (AUDIT-C)
concepts.definition: First three AUDIT items on drinking frequency, typical quantity and heavy episodes, total 0 to 12, used as a brief alcohol screen.
concepts.client_wording: Three questions about how often and how much you drink.
concepts.example: Positive AUDIT-C prompts the full AUDIT.
concepts.licensing_note: Derived from the WHO AUDIT; freely usable.

concepts.label: Drug Abuse Screening Test-10 (DAST-10)
concepts.definition: Ten yes or no items on consequences of drug use (excluding alcohol and tobacco) over the past 12 months, total 0 to 10.
concepts.client_wording: Ten yes or no questions about drug use and its effects over the past year.
concepts.example: Score 6 (substantial level) leads to fuller substance use assessment.
concepts.licensing_note: Copyright H. A. Skinner and CAMH; may be reproduced for non-commercial clinical, research and training use with credit.

concepts.label: Work and Social Adjustment Scale (WSAS)
concepts.definition: Five-item self-report of impairment attributed to the main problem in work, home management, social leisure, private leisure and relationships, each 0 to 8.
concepts.client_wording: Five questions about how much your problem affects work, home life, leisure and relationships.
concepts.example: Score 24 at intake shows marked impairment; 9 at discharge.
concepts.licensing_note: Copyright held by the authors; widely used in routine services; confirm permission for reproduction.

concepts.label: CORE-10
concepts.definition: Ten-item self-report of general psychological distress over the past week, covering anxiety, depression, functioning and risk; total 0 to 40.
concepts.client_wording: Ten questions about how you have been feeling and coping over the last week.
concepts.example: Score drops from 24 to 9, crossing the clinical cutpoint.
concepts.licensing_note: Copyright CORE System Trust; free to copy for use if unaltered; not for sale.

concepts.label: Difficulties in Emotion Regulation Scale (DERS)
concepts.definition: Thirty-six-item self-report of emotion regulation difficulties: nonacceptance, goals, impulse control, awareness, strategies and clarity.
concepts.client_wording: Questions about how you notice, understand and manage strong emotions.
concepts.example: High impulse and strategies subscales support adding DBT-informed skills.
concepts.licensing_note: Published in the validation article; free for clinical and research use with citation.

concepts.label: Ruminative Responses Scale (RRS)
concepts.definition: Twenty-two-item self-report of the tendency to ruminate in response to low mood, with brooding and reflection subscales.
concepts.client_wording: Questions about what you tend to do and think when you feel down.
concepts.example: High brooding score supports rumination-focused work.
concepts.licensing_note: Published in the research literature; free for clinical and research use with citation.

concepts.label: Outcome Rating Scale (ORS)
concepts.definition: Four visual analog scales rating individual, interpersonal, social and overall wellbeing, total 0 to 40, given at the start of each session.
concepts.client_wording: Four quick lines to mark how you have been doing in different areas of life.
concepts.example: ORS score is below the clinical cutoff and has not improved by session 4, prompting a review.
concepts.licensing_note: Free individual license for paper use; digital use requires a licensed vendor.
concepts.population: Adults; child and young child versions exist

concepts.label: Session Rating Scale (SRS)
concepts.definition: Four visual analog scales rating the session's relationship, goals and topics, approach or method, and overall fit, total 0 to 40.
concepts.client_wording: Four quick lines to tell me how today's session worked for you.
concepts.example: A lower approach rating leads the therapist to ask what would work better next time.
concepts.licensing_note: Free individual license for paper use; digital use requires a licensed vendor.

concepts.label: Working Alliance Inventory-Short Revised (WAI-SR)
concepts.definition: Twelve-item client-rated measure of the therapeutic alliance with goal, task and bond subscales, based on Bordin's model.
concepts.client_wording: Questions about how well you and your therapist are working together.
concepts.example: Low task subscale prompts a discussion about how homework is set.
concepts.licensing_note: Published in the research literature; confirm terms with the authors.
concepts.population: Adult clients; therapist and observer versions exist

concepts.label: Cognitive Therapy Scale-Revised (CTS-R)
concepts.definition: Twelve-item observer-rated scale of CBT therapist competence, each item 0 to 6, covering structure, relationship and change techniques.
concepts.client_wording: A rating of how the therapist delivered CBT in a recorded session, used in training.
concepts.example: A supervisor rates a recorded session and identifies guided discovery as the skill to develop.
concepts.licensing_note: Developed at Newcastle; freely available for training and research use with citation.
concepts.population: CBT therapists in training and supervision

concepts.label: Columbia-Suicide Severity Rating Scale (C-SSRS)
concepts.definition: Structured questions on suicidal ideation, its intensity, preparatory behavior and attempts; the screener asks 2 to 6 questions depending on answers.
concepts.client_wording: Direct questions about thoughts of suicide and any steps taken, so we can keep you safe.
concepts.example: Screener positive for recent ideation with intent, so same-day safety planning and escalation follow.
concepts.licensing_note: Free for community, healthcare and nonprofit research use; commercial use needs a license.
concepts.population: All ages; versions for different settings

concepts.label: Subjective Units of Distress Scale (SUDS)
concepts.definition: Single client rating of current distress or fear from 0 to 100, used to build hierarchies and track within-task change.
concepts.client_wording: A 0 to 100 rating of how upset or anxious you feel right now.
concepts.example: SUDS 75 at the start of exposure and 40 at the end.
concepts.licensing_note: Technique, not a copyrighted form.

concepts.label: Goal-based outcomes (GBO)
concepts.definition: Client rates progress toward up to three personally chosen goals on a 0 to 10 scale at intake and review.
concepts.client_wording: Rating how close you are to each of your own goals, from 0 to 10.
concepts.example: "Go to school every day" moves from 2 to 7 by session 10.
concepts.licensing_note: Freely available guidance from CORC; free to use with attribution.
